Hi Karthik / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at AmpleHealth is aligned on doing a short evaluation (4 weeks) before we commit to Dedicated. To help our execs greenlight spend, we need a concise Mutual Action Plan that spells out:

- Specific acceptance tasks (who verifies what)
- Concrete pass/fail triggers (metric thresholds + sample size)
- Exit gates and what happens on fail (rollback / extended pilot / credits)
- Stakeholder ledger (who signs off from our side + SLO owner)

I've attached a one-page list of our internal reviewers and procurement timelines. Can you send a draft MAP and an acceptance-tests checklist we can circulate? Our procurement deadline is 10/09, but we'd like the evaluation to finish by 09/30.

Thanks,

Alice — really appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a draft MAP (MAP-v1.xlsx) and a short timeline that maps evaluation tasks to owners. High-level proposal:

Week 0 (9/13–9/19): integration + smoke tests (engineering)
Week 1 (9/20–9/26): functional acceptance — 1k sample interactions, automated quality checks
Week 2 (9/27–10/03): performance / latency SLO validation + cost-per-token assessment
Week 3 (10/04–10/10): security/compliance evidence review + executive signoff window

Acceptance triggers (draft):
- Quality: >= 92% pass rate on rubric A across 1k labeled samples
- Latency: p95 inference <= 220ms in production-like load
- Reliability: no more than 1 critical incident (5+ min outage) during the run

Exit gates: immediate rollback if quality < 85% OR >3 critical incidents; otherwise extended pilot by mutual consent.

Owners (draft):
- Integration / engineering: Karthik Iyer
- Quality / evals: Lauren Bishop
- Commercial / procurement: Aditya Rao

Next steps: Lauren, can you attach the detailed acceptance-tests-spec? Alice — if you can send the stakeholder ledger (names + roles) we'll slot them into the signoff column.

Thanks — attaching MAP-v1.xlsx.

--
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + what pass/fail looks like

Thanks Karthik — I uploaded a detailed acceptance-tests-spec.md (attached) and pasted the key pass/fail checks below so Alice can quickly share with reviewers. I'm proposing a two-tier rubric so there's a clear remediation path before an automatic fail.

Tier 1 (blocking):
- Quality: sample-level end-to-end correctness < 85% -> FAIL
- Data leakage: any PII surfaced in responses -> FAIL
- Security: failed SOC2 demo artifacts -> FAIL

Tier 2 (remediable within 5 business days):
- Quality: 85%–91.9% -> remediable (root-cause + patch + re-run 500-sample check)
- Latency: p95 220–300ms -> optimization plan + re-test
- Cost: projected token-cost > 1.3x baseline -> discuss quantization/thresholds

Acceptance tests (short list):
1) 1k labeled prompt set run through current model config; automated scoring produces pass/fail by rubric.
2) 72-hour continuous throughput run at expected RPS to validate batching and KV caching behavior; collect p50/p95/p99.
3) Structured-output validation (JSON schema conformance) on 200 examples.
4) Security evidence: access logs, KMS config screenshots, audit log sample.

Risk mitigations I recommend including in the MAP:
- Fallback routing to smaller model variant for latency spikes (pre-approved)
- Pre-staged rollback playbook with runbook owner and timing windows
- Credit schedule tied to SLA misses (we can draft in 10/10 procurement step)

Alice — attaching acceptance-tests-spec.md and a link to the rubric spreadsheet. If you approve, we'll convert MAP-v1.xlsx into a signed-playbook PDF and propose a final run schedule.

--
Lauren Bishop
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
